ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Alert: checkout-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 07:44 UTC)
Alerting service: checkout
Alert time: 2026-06-22T07:44:00Z
Data available from 2026-06-22T06:00:00Z to 2026-06-22T09:00:00Z

Evidence so far (the latest results are steps 7 onwards):
Step 1: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-06-22T08:30:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-06-22T07:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check the exact error rate pattern around the alert time.)
  Result: M-014: Change detected at 2026-06-22T07:40:00Z: mean 0.36 before, 10.19 after (123.7 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-014] checkout.error_rate_pct from 2026-06-22T07:00:00Z to 2026-06-22T08:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.21 max=10.39 mean=6.05 last=10.23; mean=6.05. Change detected at 2026-06-22T07:40:00Z: mean 0.36 before, 10.19 after (123.7 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-06-22T07:20:00Z = 0.21 (lowest); 2026-06-22T07:40:00Z = 10.15 (first point after the change); 2026-06-22T08:25:00Z = 10.39 (peak); 2026-06-22T08:30:00Z = 10.23 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"aggregation": "max", "end": "2026-06-22T08:30:00Z", "metric": "restarts", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-06-22T07:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if the service has been restarting due to OOM or crashes.)
  Result: M-018: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-018] checkout.restarts from 2026-06-22T07:00:00Z to 2026-06-22T08:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=0 max=0 mean=0 last=0; max=0. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-06-22T07:00:00Z = 0 (lowest); 2026-06-22T07:00:00Z = 0 (peak); 2026-06-22T08:30:00Z = 0 (last).
Step 3: log_search {"end": "2026-06-22T07:50:00Z", "limit": 30, "query": "deploy, migration, config, error, warn, exception", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-06-22T07:35:00Z"} (asked because: Search checkout service logs around the start of the incident for configuration, deployment, or error indicators.)
  Result: 5 matching log lines.
  [L-0294] 2026-06-22T07:42:22Z checkout WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0303] 2026-06-22T07:44:48Z checkout WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0319] 2026-06-22T07:48:10Z checkout WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0320] 2026-06-22T07:48:11Z checkout WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0323] 2026-06-22T07:48:47Z checkout WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
Step 4: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-06-22T08:30:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-06-22T07:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if database connection pool is exhausted during the incident.)
  Result: M-012: Change detected at 2026-06-22T07:25:00Z: mean 30.35 before, 73.5 after (25.5 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-012] checkout.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-06-22T07:00:00Z to 2026-06-22T08:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=26.01 max=99.35 mean=62.14 last=99.35; mean=62.14. Change detected at 2026-06-22T07:25:00Z: mean 30.35 before, 73.5 after (25.5 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-06-22T07:25:00Z = 26.01 (first point after the change); 2026-06-22T07:25:00Z = 26.01 (lowest); 2026-06-22T08:30:00Z = 99.35 (last); 2026-06-22T08:30:00Z = 99.35 (peak).
Step 5: metrics_query {"aggregation": "mean", "end": "2026-06-22T08:30:00Z", "metric": "cpu_pct", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-06-22T07:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if CPU usage changed abruptly during the incident.)
  Result: M-011: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-011] checkout.cpu_pct from 2026-06-22T07:00:00Z to 2026-06-22T08:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=33.42 max=43.49 mean=38.64 last=43.49; mean=38.64. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-06-22T07:40:00Z = 33.42 (lowest); 2026-06-22T08:30:00Z = 43.49 (last); 2026-06-22T08:30:00Z = 43.49 (peak).
Step 6: log_search {"end": "2026-06-22T07:45:00Z", "limit": 30, "query": "version, deploy, start, init, config, env", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-06-22T07:30:00Z"} (asked because: Search for deployment or startup logs just before the error spike to check for bad_deployment or misconfiguration.)
  Result: 0 matching log lines.
Step 7: log_search {"end": "2026-06-22T07:45:00Z", "level": "WARN", "limit": 30, "query": "pool, connection, database, timeout, SQL", "service": "checkout", "start": "2026-06-22T07:25:00Z"} (asked because: Check logs for database connection pool exhaustion or timeout errors right around when pool usage started increasing.)
  Result: 1 matching log lines.
  [L-0284] 2026-06-22T07:40:14Z checkout WARN cache miss ratio 98%, falling back to database key=product:2829
Step 8: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "database connection pool exhaustion mitigation steps"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance for db_connection_pool_exhaustion to get mitigation steps before concluding.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-02-7 (similarity 0.84).
  [R-02-7] Database connection pool exhaustion - Escalation (similarity 0.84): Call the database team if the database itself is close to its connection limit or is refusing new connections, since raising pool sizes elsewhere will then make things worse. Share the pool graphs so they can see which services hold the most connections.
  [R-02-5] Database connection pool exhaustion - Mitigation (similarity 0.80): Restart the affected instances to release held connections as a first step. Then raise the pool maximum, staying inside the database's own connection limit, and shed non-essential traffic. If connections are leaking, find the code path that does not return them.
  [R-02-6] Database connection pool exhaustion - Verify recovery (similarity 0.77): Pool usage should fall well below its maximum, the number of waiting requests should drop to zero and latency should return to normal within a few minutes. Watch it for half an hour in case the pool fills again.

Previous hypotheses:
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: Database connection pool usage significantly increased starting at 07:25 UTC and reached nearly 100% by 08:30 UTC, directly correlating with the elevated error rates starting at 07:40 UTC. (evidence: M-012, M-014)
- slow_query_missing_index: Database pool exhaustion can be triggered by slow queries holding onto connections longer than usual, causing requests to back up and elevate error rates. (evidence: M-012, M-014)
- downstream_timeout: Downstream dependencies taking longer to respond can tie up database connections and cause request timeouts and errors in the checkout service. (evidence: M-012, M-014)
